head: joint_render

bar.rule: NON-INFERIORITY, and it is a ratified deviation from this project's winner rule. The candidate is viable iff no gated arm is significantly worse than that kind's shipped head. Nothing is required to be better: the declared benefit is one head instead of two, which no sheet can measure
bar.significance: 95 percent paired cluster bootstrap, 5000 draws at seed 0, resampling whole neighbourhood groups under the exact non-`c` rule. Both heads are scored on the same resampled rows, so the population's own difficulty cancels

arms.why: the proper scoring rule on the smooth eval split, over all three cutpoints. This head's interface is its probabilities and a floor is a point on one of them

refused.strange_auc_ge4: blind_modes is never read at >=4. Its only four positives at that boundary are four rows a later ANCHORED pass revised up from 3, having seen a tier; they are the sheet's four superseded rows. An AUC over them is an AUC over the only non-blind rows on a blind sheet
refused.smooth_auc_ge2: blind_minibrot holds no tier-1 row, so its >=2 boundary has no negative class and its AUC there is undefined rather than perfect

gain_on_the_smooth_side.caveat: the candidate saw 160 smooth rows the shipped smooth head never did, so a BETTER here is transfer OR corpus growth. The corpus-matched ablation is the arm that separates them

scale_against_order.what_it_is: REPORTED, never gated. Each cutpoint's cross-entropy split into what an in-sample isotonic recalibration removes (the scale) and what survives it (the order). The same fit the release floors are placed by, so a gap that lives in the scale term is a gap adoption re-derives anyway

smooth_render.unreadable: the sheet holds only one class here

against_the_corpus_matched_ablation.what_it_is: one kind's share of exactly the pooled split, at exactly the candidate's recipe. Paired seed for seed against the candidate, so the only thing that moves is whether the other kind's rows were in the batch. NO BAR is attached

arms.no_band_because: 2 ablation run(s) against 3 candidate run(s): a median needs three. The seed-for-seed pairs are the read
